feedback: Encourage the child to put the courage and teamwork in their own words rather than just naming facts.
If the dialogue stalls, offer a gentle prompt such as 'What did the crew eat?' or 'Why didn't they give up?'
activities.intendedInsight: Leadership and care for the team — not reaching the goal — are what make Shackleton remembered as brave.
learnerActions: Pretend to talk with a warm, friendly Shackleton and ask how he kept his men going when the ship was lost.
Ask him what the hardest and coldest moments were, and how the team helped each other.
Say back in your own words one thing Shackleton did to bring everyone home.
activities.title: Talking with Shackleton (spoken role-play extension)

feedback: If a child muddles who did what, re-sort the three cards slowly, saying each explorer's one memorable fact aloud.

If a child says Amundsen 'just got lucky', compare choices: his skilled use of dog sleds and skis and careful supply planning versus Scott's reliance on ponies, motor sledges that broke down, and men pulling heavy sledges themselves — preparation and choices mattered a lot (though weather and other factors played a part too).
If a child calls Shackleton's trip 'just a disaster', refocus on the outcome that made it legendary: the ship was lost but every crew member came home alive.
activities.intendedInsight: Children can keep the three stories distinct and tie each explorer to his outcome, while still holding onto the point that getting the team home mattered as much as reaching the Pole.
learnerActions: Sort three portrait cards — Amundsen, Scott, Shackleton — each with one memorable fact.
Match each explorer to his story: Amundsen (first to the Pole), Scott (reached it, died returning), Shackleton (ship crushed, saved all of the Endurance crew).
Name at least one thing that made polar exploration hard: freezing cold, running short of food, or thick ice.
Say in one sentence why Shackleton is remembered as brave even though he never reached his goal.
activities.title: Who did what? (sorting to firm up recall)
